For a measurable \(A\subset {\mathbb {R}}^n\) with \(\lambda (A)<\infty ,\) where \(\lambda \) denotes the Lebesgue measure, its Schwarz symmetrization (or rearrangement) \(A^*\) is the open ball centered at the origin such that \(\lambda (A)=\lambda (A^*). # Rearrangements and the Monge–Ampère equations * Open access * Published: 06 August 2024 * Volume 308, article number 17 (2024) * Cite this article You have full access to this open access article Download PDF Save article View saved research Mathematische Zeitschrift Aims and scope Submit manuscript (mathzeit@math.toronto.edu) Rearrangements and the Monge–Ampère equations Download PDF * Zbigniew Błocki^{1}  * 1134 Accesses * Explore all metrics ## Abstract We show that the direct counterpart of the Talenti symmetrization estimate for the Laplacian does not hold neither for the complex nor real Monge–Ampère equations. We also use this Talenti result to improve some known estimates for subharmonic functions in \({\mathbb {C}},\) where the constant depends on the area of the domain, instead of the diameter. We refer to [7] for a good introduction to the topic of rearrangements. The main result from the viewpoint of PDEs is the following theorem due to Talenti [18]: if \(\Omega \) is a bounded domain in \({\mathbb {R}}^n,\) \(f\ge 0\) and u, v solve the Dirichlet problems: $$\begin{aligned} {\left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \Delta u=f&{}\text {in }\Omega \\ u=0&{}\text {on }\partial \Omega \end{array}\right. } \quad {\left\{ \begin{array}{ll} \Delta v=f^*&{}\text {in }\Omega ^*\\ v=0&{}\text {on }\partial \Omega ^*, \end{array}\right. } \end{aligned}$$ then \(v\le u^*.\) The main tool in the proof is the isoperimetric inequality. One should note that in general \(u^*\) need not be subharmonic: as noticed in [3], if u is the Green function for a disc with pole away from the center then \(u^*\) is not subharmonic (this example is due to P. Thomas). The Talenti estimate has many applications, it for example immediately gives various optimal bounds for subharmonic functions. We present them in Sect. 2, including improved estimates of Brezis–Merle [6] and Benelkourchi–Jennane–Zeriahi [2]. One could ask a similar question for the complex Monge–Ampère equation (CMA): assume that \(\Omega \) is a bounded domain in \({\mathbb {C}}^n,\) \(f\in C(\overline{\Omega }),\) \(f\ge 0,\) and u, v solve the following Dirichlet problems: $$\begin{aligned} {\left\{ \begin{array}{ll} u\in PSH\cap C(\Omega ) &{}\\ (dd^cu)^n=f\,d\lambda &{}\text {in }\Omega \\ u=0&{}\text {on }\partial \Omega \end{array}\right. } \quad {\left\{ \begin{array}{ll} v\in PSH\cap C(\Omega ^*) &{}\\ (dd^cv)^n=f^*\,d\lambda &{}\text {in }\Omega ^*\\ v=0&{}\text {on }\partial \Omega ^*. \end{array}\right. } \end{aligned}$$ (2) Recall that \(d=\partial +\overline{\partial },\) \(d^c=i(\overline{\partial }-\partial )\) (see e.g. [9] or [11] for precise definitions of the operators \(\partial \) and \(\overline{\partial }\)). We then have \(dd^c=2i\partial \overline{\partial }\) and for a smooth u $$\begin{aligned} (dd^cu)^n=4^nn!\det (u_{j\bar{k}})\, d\lambda , \end{aligned}$$ where \(u_{j\bar{k}}=\partial ^2u/\partial z_j\partial \overline{z}_k.\) In case of (2) \(\Omega \) has to be pseudoconvex, that is it admits a plurisubharmonic (psh) exhaustion (see e.g. [11]), or even hyperconvex, that is this psh exhaustion vanishes on \(\partial \Omega \) (see e.g. [4]). By [1] \((dd^u)^n\) makes sense as a measure for continuous psh u and by [1, 4] we have existence of appropriate weak solutions to this Dirichlet problem. New continuous solutions to Monge-Ampère equations on Hermitian manifolds SŁAWOMIR KOŁODZIEJ (joint work with Cuong Ngoc Nguyen) We prove the existence of a continuous quasi-plurisubharmonic solution to Monge-Ampère equations with very general the right hand side on a compact Hermitian manifold. These are measures dominated by capacity, in particular, moderate measures studied by Dinh-Nguyen-Sibony. As a consequence, we give a characterization of measures admitting Hölder continuous quasi-plurisubharmonic potential, inspired from the work of Dinh-Nguyen. The setting is as follows: a compact Hermitian manifold \((X,\omega)\) of dimension \(n\). The fundamental form \(\omega\) is given in local coordinates by \[ \omega = \frac{i}{2}\sum_{k,j} g_{k\bar{j}}\,dz^k \wedge d\bar{z}^j. \] The matrix \((g_{k\bar{j}})\) is positive definite and Hermitian symmetric. Such a form exists on any complex manifold, which is not the case for Kähler forms \(d\omega = 0\). An upper semicontinuous function \(u\) on \(X\) is called \(\omega\)-psh if \(dd^c u + \omega \ge 0\) (as currents). Then we write \(u \in PSH(\omega)\). Consider a positive Radon measure \(\mu\) with finite total mass on \(X\). To solve the complex Monge-Ampère equation for \(\mu\) we need to find an \(\omega\)-psh function \(u\) and a positive constant \(c\) such that \[ (\omega + dd^c u)^n = c\,\mu. \] For smooth, strictly positive measures Cherrier (1987) obtained smooth solutions of the M-A equation assuming either \(n=2\) or that \(\omega\) is balanced \((d(\omega^{n-1})=0)\).
